text:
marta: ran a focused profile on host parse + streaming path. cpu time dominated by small syscall writes in grpc writev and tokenize loop. trace attached: https://s3.redwood/profiles/3245678901/ingress-flame.svg
kevin: can you paste the flame? curious whether kernel selection or tokenization is the main culprit
marta: quick flame snippet pasted inline: ```flamegraph.svg  CPU  120ms
  host_parse -> tokenize_loop -> writev -> kvcache.lookup```
but top-level hotspot is `tokenize_one_byte` with lots of tiny allocations and memmoves
liam: allocations in tokenization are surprising. are we still doing per-token string copies in the parse loop? we should try reusing a single buffer slice and emitting offsets
sara: fwiw gRPC/HTTP2 framing adds ~30-60us per stream when we emit lots of sub-1k frames. small writes + HPACK overhead compounds at high qps
kevin: idea: change streaming coalescing heuristics to target a byte threshold (e.g. 4k or 8k) or a token-count threshold before doing a write. that will reduce syscall frequency without changing model behavior
marta: ran a canary with `coalesce_size_bytes=8192` and `stream_max_delay_ms=2`. p95 tail latency down ~18% on ingest host, but p50 for <50 token requests increased ~2-3ms for lat-sensitive benchmarks
liam: expected tradeoff. alternative: keep smaller coalesce_size, but optimize tokenization to remove allocations and early proto serialization so we don't serialize twice
sara: KV cache gotchas: we synchronously `kvcache.lookup` inside tokenize path for prefix hits. that blocks parse->write path. switching to async lookup (fire-and-forget + attach on ready) looks promising
marta: PoC async-kvcache: spawn lookup future while tokenizing, attach KV result to outgoing stream when done. microbench shows ~12% CPU drop on hot ingress nodes and fewer syscall bursts
kevin: excellent. let's capture these as action items: 1) PR for tokenize buffer reuse + zero-copy offsets, 2) change proto serialize order to avoid duplicate writes, 3) default coalesce to 4k with 1ms max_delay for canary, 4) RFC + implement async kvcache lookup, 5) gRPC microbench to measure smallwrite vs kernel selection impact for seq_len<64
sara: and add a benchmark that reproduces HPACK overhead: simulate many 1k streaming frames across HTTP/2 to see net syscall vs kernel benefit. some kernels are faster for <64 seq but lose to syscall overhead, so we need both sides measured
liam: pinging @eng-sre for canary infra and @product to surface perf vs latency tradeoffs for customers
ops-bot: canary job created: canary-3245678901-1, scheduled across 3 zones
marta: opening the PRs and RFC now, will paste links when ready
kevin: thanks all. nice and pragmatic plan. :thumbsup:
